column3: “Answered and said” is rendered “answered.”
“Thus” is rendered “this is so.”
“Desires to conduct a case” is rendered “wished to dispute.” It is unclear in the Hebrew who cannot answer whom.
“Shown stubbornness to him and remained unharmed” is rendered “defied Him without harm.”
NASB supplies “It is God” and “how.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Speaks to the sun and it does not shine” is rendered “commands the sun not to shine.”
“The high places of the sea” is rendered “the waves of the sea”; it may mean “the back of the sea.”
The identity of the star names is uncertain.
“Until there is not inquiry” is rendered “unfathomable.”
“There!” is rendered as a condition (“Were He to”).
“There!” is rendered “Were He to”; “turn him back” is rendered “restrain Him.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Indeed? for I” is rendered “How then can I.”
“To my judge I will seek favor” is rendered “I would have to implore the mercy of my judge.”
“Not I believe” is rendered “I could not believe.”
“A storm” is rendered “a tempest”; the word may also mean “a hair.”
“Surfeits” is rendered “saturates.”
The Hebrew reads “who will summon me”; NASB reads “summon Him.” NASB supplies “it is a matter of.”
The Hebrew reads “it declared me guilty” (my mouth); NASB has “He will declare me guilty.”
“I do not know myself” is rendered “I do not take notice of myself.”
“Bringing to an end” is rendered “destroys.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“A land” is rendered “The earth.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Ships of reed” is rendered “reed boats.”
“Let loose my face” is rendered “leave off my sad countenance.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“I will be guilty” is rendered “I am accounted wicked.”
The written text reads “with water of snow”; NASB follows the reading “with snow.” “Potash” is rendered “lye.”
